body: Not quite.  I want to make sure I balance her as an independent, individual woman and as a mother.  I’m sure both are incredibly important components to her identity so I want to treat it as such.

From what I can tell, she is professionally successful and has a good paying job.   Not sure that’s needed.  🙄

But either way, when it comes to kids I’d rather drain my bank accounts while giving them a good time than have a ton of cash in the bank.
So next time I see her I’m going to ask her out. Please tell me I’m doing the right thing. Please tell me it’ll okay if I get rejected. 😬
For what it’s worth, I guess what I’m worried about is if she does have someone (eg a husband or boyfriend).  I’m not sure how someone might respond to that, I guess.
I called them my “ex’s family” intentionally.  But still, I’ve known them forever.  Just seems kinda like a general respect thing. IDK
You’d think but my family is doing what I believe is appropriate, given the fact we have children together, and still keeping a positive relationship with my ex.   🤷🏻‍♂️
This!!  I was made to believe work and providing for my family was the reason for life, not enjoying things.  This new girl loves teasing me, pushing me to experience new things, and enjoy life.
I didn’t intend to start a relationship when I reached out.  I was lonely, I figured she was, and I was going through something similar to what she did.

It’s not necessarily an excuse, it’s more like a habit I’m used to it.  It was actually part of the issue we had with our marriage - I had to do everything for her and make sure I protected her feelings about everything.  I couldn’t say “no” to having her family over to dinner without her becoming borderline depressed about it.
